cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California's 23rd Congressional District in 2026. A Licensed Clinical Social Worker with almost a decade of experience working with vulnerable populations, including foster children and students. She has also worked for San Bernardino County, incorporating state and federal legislation into county policy. She has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Endorsements Hodge lists in her Ballotpedia survey: Teamsters Local 1932, Assembly Member Dr. Corey Jackson, Mayor of Big Bear Lake Randall Putz, Mayor of Moreno Valley Ulises Cabrera, Southern California Armenian Democrats, Democrats of the Morongo Basin, Big Bear Democratic Club, and Redlands Area Democratic Club.
Ballotpedia lists the Democratic Party of California, San Bernardino Young Democrats and California Young Democrats among her endorsements.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Hodge holding public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no documented statements from her on data centers, property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, growth limits, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign issues page lists topics such as humane immigration policy, protecting the environment and public education, but the detail under each heading was not readable. She says she supports Medicare for all, affordable housing, protecting renters and cutting red tape on housing costs, and getting big money out of politics, but she gave no specific pledges on these. We found no news coverage or controversies about her. Her birthplace is described only as within the district, with no city given.

cands.bio: Republican U.S. Representative for California's 23rd District since 2021. Founder and owner of FarSight Studios, a video game developer. Previously a Big Bear City airport board member, Big Bear Lake city councilman and mayor, and California Assemblymember (2014-2020). Holds degrees from Caltech, UCLA and California Baptist University.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $1,632 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.
Missed 15 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (2.2%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 12, 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-03.

On Jan. 6–7, 2021, Obernolte voted to object to counting Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes. In a Jan. 5 statement he said he would back objections where election rules were changed by courts or executives without the state legislature's consent. He called this a constitutional, nonpartisan position.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in 2026 by President Donald Trump and the Republican Party of California.

His campaign site lists endorsements from San Bernardino County Sheriff Shannon Dicus, District Attorney Jason Anderson, California Professional Firefighters, the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance by him on data centers or on development limits. We found no record of how he has acted on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, school choice, gun laws, or H-1B visas. The sources do not say when he moved to California. His own campaign site was the only source for several of his stated positions.

votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

qual.background: Served on the Big Bear Lake city council (2010-2014, mayor 2012-2014), six years in the California State Assembly (including as vice chair of the Budget Committee), and has been in the U.S. House since 2021. He also founded and runs a software company and holds a doctorate in public administration with a dissertation on executive-legislative budget conflict.
qual.why: Extensive prior legislative and local executive office, including state budget work, plus business management and a policy-focused doctorate, fits the high band for a lawmaking, oversight and budgeting role.

pro-life.evidence: Supported the overturning of Roe v. Wade and believes that because the Constitution does not mention abortion, states may outlaw it.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Yea on the Laken Riley Act, which requires DHS to detain certain people in the U.S. without legal permission who are arrested for burglary, theft, larceny or shoplifting (passed 263-156, signed Jan. 29, 2025).

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he authored legislation to hold fentanyl dealers accountable for poisoning children.
